title: `@libs/mobile-components`
subject: ui
summary: The mobile UI library: React Native components on the same contract as `@libs/web-components`. The rationale is in `DESIGN.md` (`./DESIGN.md`).

purpose.intro: The mobile UI library: React Native components on the same contract as `@libs/web-components`. The rationale is in `DESIGN.md` (`./DESIGN.md`).

claims.text: A mobile component is one element of that table. It has the same name as its web twin and the same axis props: `emphasis`, `status`, `scale`, `state`. Its first line says which element it is and which web component, at which version, it mirrors.
The code is not shared. The web component renders HTML and is styled by CSS; this one renders React Native views and reads its style from the native theme.

reference.statement: One table rules both libraries: `shared/libs/ui/types/elements.ts`. Each row is an element, with its family, the platforms it exists on, and the values it takes on each axis.

snippets.code:
import { ThemeProvider, Button, Card, Badge, Text } from "@libs/mobile-components";
import { Stack } from "@libs/mobile-layouts";
import theme from "<themes>/bounx-mobile/v1/generated/bounx-mobile.native.json";

<ThemeProvider theme={theme} mode="light">
  <Card>
    <Stack dir="row" align="center" justify="between" gap={12}>
      <Stack gap={4} size="fill">
        <Badge>Group session</Badge>
        <Text type="heading4">Junior Squad</Text>
      </Stack>
      <Button scale="sm">Start</Button>
    </Stack>
  </Card>
</ThemeProvider>

claims.text: Every interactive component sets its accessibility role and state, and passes the native props of the React Native component it wraps.

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Component | Element | Web twin |
|---|---|---|
| `Button` | `control--button` | Button |
| `Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardContent`, `CardFooter` | `surface--card`, `--header`, `--content`, `--footer` | Card and its regions |
| `Badge` | `surface--badge` | Badge |
| `Avatar` | `surface--avatar` | Avatar |
| `Input` | `field--input` | Input |
| `PhoneInput` | `field--phone-input` | PhoneInput |
| `Field`, `Label` | `surface--label`, `--field-description`, `--field-message` | Label and the field wrappers |
| `ChoiceGroup` | `control-group--choice-group` with `control--toggle` | the choice group |
| `Group` | `surface--group` | a titled section |
| `EmptyState` | `surface--empty-state` | EmptyState |
| `Icon` | `shape--icon` | Icon, same semantic names, same icon set (Lucide) |
| `Text` | the typography levels, `type--<level>` | the `type--*` attribute |
| `Stepper` | a composite of `button-group`, `button`, `button-group-text` | none: mobile's own |

claims.text: `ThemeProvider` takes a native theme (the `<id>.native.json` the mobile theme engine writes) and a colour mode.
`useElement(element, axes)` returns the element's style for its axes: `{ view, text, color, icon, extras }`.
`usePart(element, part, axes)` does the same for a surface inside an element (a list's row, a switch's thumb).
`useType(level)` and `useColor(name)` read a typography level and a colour.
A component never writes a colour, a size or a spacing of its own.

reference.statement: A component is themed only by reading the theme. There is no cascade in React Native.

`active` (pressed), `focus`, `selected`, `disabled`, `loading` are shared with the web. `long-pressed` and `swiped` are mobile's. There is no `hover`. A component computes its states from what happens to it and also accepts `state` to force one.
